1278: Family-owned campground at 959 CR 111 E, Rushsylvania, nine miles north of Bellefontaine and 12 miles east of Indian Lake, open May 1 to October 25 in 2026: 82 sites, all with 30-amp electric and water, 32 of them for overnight stays and the rest seasonal, among them twelve gravel-and-cement back-in pads and grass buddy sites.  It has two ponds, one for swimming and catch-and-release fishing, a lodge with a general store, a shower house, a dump station, hiking trails, a dog run and a playground.  The entry gate is staffed and closes overnight, from 9 p.m. Sunday to Thursday and from 10 p.m. on Friday and Saturday. --Claude
1521: Motel and campground at 593 Route 8, Bridgewater, on a 6-acre private lake with a sandy beach, the lake and a brook both stocked for fishing: 67 campsites, 17 of them with 30/50-amp electric and water, 10 with full hookups and 40 for tents, plus 6 cabins and the motel.  There are hot showers, a laundromat, a camp store, a dump station and honey-wagon service, and paddle boats, canoes and kayaks; pets are welcome but not on the beach or in the lake. --Claude
1737: Family campground at 24832 Rock Falls Road, Sterling, open since 1965, with 30/50-amp RV sites up to 40 ft and tent sites.  It has a swimming pool, open to the public from late May to Labor Day, a general store, an arcade, creek fishing, a laundry and a dump station. --Claude
1982: Family-owned park at 1501 N. Osage Blvd, Nevada, near I-49 and Highway 54, open year round: 30- and 50-amp full-hookup sites, some shaded, with picnic tables and fire pits.  There are showers, a laundry open around the clock, a general store and RV supplies, propane, a playground, a seasonal pool, and horse stalls and a corral for guests travelling with horses. --Claude
2230: Private park at 30370 NE 30th St, northeast of Pratt, next door to Bert's RV Park: full- and partial-hookup 30/50-amp sites, primitive RV sites and tent sites, with picnic tables, fire rings and grills, shade, a petting zoo and a dump station. --Claude
2661: City of Rifle park, not the neighbouring Rifle Falls State Park, in a limestone canyon along East Rifle Creek, reached by a gravel road past the fish hatchery at the end of Highway 325, with over 250 bolted climbing routes.  Its primitive campsites are first come, first served or reserved online, the 14 Huffman Gulch sites staying first come, first served; sites marked Van take no trailers, and every vehicle must show a day or annual pass.  A 23-ft rig fits the larger drive-in sites. --Claude
2879: Year-round RV park at 2005 US Highway 183, Elm Creek, half a mile north of I-80's exit 257: 38 pull-through sites with 30/50-amp full hookups, long enough for an RV up to 100 ft to stay hitched.  There are private showers and bathrooms, a laundry, free Wi-Fi and a dog park. --Claude
3238: RV park at 708 South Iris Street, Mount Pleasant, at the Highway 34 and 218 interchange, built in 2006 and open year round: full-hookup 30/50-amp sites, pull-throughs among them, with Wi-Fi.  There are private bathrooms, a laundry open around the clock, a dump station, a store, a playground and a meeting room, and up to 2 pets are welcome; trains pass about a quarter mile away. --Claude
3375: Campground on the Sugar River at N4697 County Road E, Brodhead, near the Sugar River State Trail, with back-in RV sites (electric only, or electric and water), tent and group sites, and seasonal sites.  There are community restrooms and showers and a dump station; campers fish from the riverbank, and tubes, canoes and kayaks are rented with a free shuttle. --Claude
3488: Sheboygan County's most popular park, on the Sheboygan Marsh at W7039 County Highway SR near Elkhart Lake, its campground run by Three Guys & a Grill from the Marsh Lodge restaurant and tavern on site.  The 50 RV sites have water and 30/50-amp electric, back-in and pull-through, beside overflow sites and a tent area; there are showers, a dump station, a launch ramp, fishing piers and the state's tallest wooden observation tower. --Claude
4090: Dowley family campground at 16 Kenolie Campground, Newfane, open April 10 to October 25 in 2026, with water and 30- or 50-amp electric at its RV sites, room for RVs and trailers up to 40 ft, wooded and open sites, and seasonal and monthly rentals; tent sites and the one lean-to take stays of up to 14 days.  There are flush toilets, hot showers, a laundry room, a dump station, a small store and limited Wi-Fi, but no TV.  The West River is within walking distance, but the campground sits back from it. --Claude
4634: Family-owned RV park on 16 wooded acres at 980 Honeysuckle Rd, Dublin, off I-16's exit 49, opened in 2021: pull-through and back-in sites, most with a concrete patio, all with 30/50-amp electric, city water, sewer and Wi-Fi, for overnight and long-term stays.  Every overnight site is a pull-through, and late arrivals self-register at the office door.  There is a coin laundry and a big off-leash dog park, but no restrooms. --Claude
